prompt: A Ferris wheel has diameter $40$ m, its lowest seat is $2$ m above the ground, and it takes $60$ seconds per turn. You board at the lowest point at $t = 0$. Which equation gives your height $h$, in metres, after $t$ seconds?
hint: Radius is half the diameter, and the centre sits one radius above the lowest seat.

hints.text: Radius is half the diameter, and the centre sits one radius above the lowest seat.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up on a smaller wheel: diameter $10$, lowest seat $1$ m, one turn in $20$ s gives radius $5$, midline $1 + 5 = 6$, and $B = \frac{2\pi}{20} = \frac{\pi}{10}$, so $h = 6 - 5\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{10}\right)$. Build yours from the same four pieces.
Starting at the BOTTOM needs a flipped cosine: $h = 22 - 20\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{30}\right)$.

explanation: The radius is $\frac{40}{2} = 20$ m, so the amplitude is $20$.
The centre of the wheel is one radius above the lowest seat: $2 + 20 = 22$ m, which is the midline.
One turn takes $60$ s, so $\frac{2\pi}{B} = 60$ and $B = \frac{\pi}{30}$.
At $t = 0$ you are at the minimum, and a negative cosine starts at its minimum: $h = 22 - 20\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{30}\right)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test $t = 0$ and $t = 30$
steps: At $t = 0$ choice A gives $22 - 20(1) = 2$ m — the boarding platform. Correct.
At $t = 30$ (half a turn) it gives $22 - 20(-1) = 42$ m, which is $2 + 40$, the very top. Correct.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: The tempting wrong answer is B, $h = 22 + 20\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{30}\right)$, because $+\cos$ looks like the "normal" choice.
But test it: at $t = 0$ it gives $22 + 20 = 42$ m, which would mean you boarded at the top of the wheel, forty metres up.
Always plug in $t = 0$ and check it against where the story says you start. A plain cosine starts at the MAXIMUM; if the story starts you at the minimum, you need the minus sign.
